description: Trying to detect anomalies in earth phenomenons
summary: As Team Bozkurt, we investigated the background of the 2021 mucilage outbreak in the Sea of Marmara by combining NASA satellite data with field studies by Turkish scientists. Because of its two-layer structure, the Marmara flushes out pollution slowly, and it has warmed by about 1 °C over the past 17 years. NASA MODIS-Aqua data show that chlorophyll-a in İzmit Bay is nearly eight times higher than in the open sea. The main nutrient sources are Black Sea inflow and Istanbul’s wastewater, most of which receives only pre-treatment. In 2021, the nutrient balance collapsed: species diversity fell while phytoplankton numbers surged. We recommend a satellite-based early-warning system and advanced biological wastewater treatment in Istanbul.
details:
Our project investigates why the Sea of Marmara suffered a massive mucilage outbreak in 2021 and whether satellites could have warned us earlier. We combined 17 years of NASA MODIS-Aqua chlorophyll-a data (2005–2022) with field measurements and peer-reviewed Turkish studies to map where eutrophication concentrates, identify its nutrient sources, and trace how the 2021 event affected marine biodiversity.

The results show a persistent east–west gradient: chlorophyll-a in İzmit Bay is nearly eight times higher than in the open sea. Black Sea inflow and Istanbul's mostly pre-treated wastewater supply the nutrients. Both mucilage events began in low-chlorophyll years and were followed by record highs, which suggests a detectable early signal.

The intended impact is a satellite-based early-warning system for İzmit and Gemlik bays using NASA MODIS and PACE data, together with evidence supporting advanced wastewater treatment in Istanbul.

We used NASA Giovanni for data access, and Python (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib) to process the NetCDF data, mask lakes and neighbouring seas, compute regional statistics, and build the figures. An AI assistant (Claude) supported the analysis and design.

We considered several factors carefully: coastal satellite uncertainty, spatial autocorrelation between pixels, mass versus molar nutrient ratios, and copyright. All published figures were redrawn from reported values rather than copied.
